Subject: Renewal discussion — usage review + proposed uplift options

Hi Maya / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time with our team last week. I pulled together a short usage snapshot and an initial set of commit options that map to the traffic pattern we saw in Q3–Q4. The attached "2026Q4-usage-breakdown.pdf" has the daily token cadence, model mix (chat vs embedding), and our latency percentiles.

Why this matters: your sustained embedding volume in August–October suggests predictable cost savings with reserved capacity, and the chat burst pattern (evenings/weekends) benefits from a small reserved pool plus burst credits vs pure on-demand.

As next steps, can we do a 45-minute renewal workshop the week of Dec 6 to walk options and ROI? Proposed agenda:
- Quick recap of performance & token mix (5 min)
- Three commit options + cost/latency tradeoffs (20 min)
- Migration/fallback & SLOs (10 min)
- Plan & timeline (10 min)

Attaching: 2026Q4-usage-breakdown.pdf (high level), I'll follow with a spreadsheet of the commit scenarios after internal alignment.

If you want a quick preview of the conservative/moderate/aggressive numbers, say Friday and I’ll send a short table.

Thanks,
Hannah

Maya — great questions. Short answers first:

- Token split: the attached spreadsheet (commit-options-ROI.xlsx) uses Clearview's billing export plus our normalized token mapping. Current split in our calc: embeddings 60.8%, chat generation 39.2% (close to your 62% call once normalized). I’ll include the raw mapping tab in the sheet.
- Latency spike: we see the 95th pctl uplift mid-Oct tied to a temporary model fallback on the smaller cluster during a maintenance window — not a degradation in model quality. We've flagged that and recommend the moderate/dedicated option to avoid that class of fallback.
- Preservation of current latency w/ savings: yes — Option B (moderate commit) is designed to keep your 95th pctl within current bounds while delivering ~22% cost reduction vs on-demand.

High-level commit options (numbers are annualized; see attached sheet for month-by-month):

Option A — Conservative - Commit: 1.0M embedded-equivalent tokens/month - Expected annual spend vs today: -6% - Latency: comparable, small burst credits for evenings

Option B — Moderate (recommended) - Commit: 1.6M embedded-equivalent tokens/month - Expected annual spend vs today: -22% - Latency: maintains current 95th pctl; includes 2% monthly burst buffer - Includes SLA: 99.5% uptime, 95th pctl latency target tied to credit schedule

Option C — Aggressive - Commit: 2.4M embedded-equivalent tokens/month - Expected annual spend vs today: -33% - Latency: best-in-class tier, reserved pool sizing for peak nights

Operational notes:
- Migration: we can stage the rollout by moving embedding traffic to a dedicated pool first (low-risk) and then expand chat reservations.
- Fallbacks: automatic downgrade to compatible quantized variant is configured; in the moderate option we reduce fallback probability by reserving a minimum pool.
- Contract: I'll draft a term-sheet reflecting Option B with a 12-month term + mid-year review; will attach redwood-term-sheet-v2.pdf for legal.

Can we lock the workshop for Dec 7 11:00–11:45 PT and I’ll share the deck + short ROI table beforehand? Ben and Lauren are on copy for SLA and contract items.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Looping in a quick ops note — Hannah’s analysis looks good. A couple items for the workshop deck: 

- Add a simple failure-mode slide that shows expected behavior during host maintenance (what happened Oct 14–18) and how Option B prevents the fallback.
- Offer a short canary SLA credit: if latency > target two months in a row during first quarter after go-live, we provide a one-time service credit equal to 5% of monthly committed spend. Keeps incentive tight for both parties.
- Confirm pre-wired KMS key for Clearview if they choose Dedicated (we’ll need policy and IAM lines).

Hannah — I’ll be available for the Dec 7 call, can pick up the SLA slide and the credit language.

Ben Carter

Hannah — thanks for the thorough breakdown and the deck you sent earlier. After reviewing the numbers with finance, Clearview is comfortable moving forward with Option B (moderate) pending: 

1) Updated term sheet reflecting the 12-month commitment, Option B token baselines, and the two-week notice cadence for burst credits.
2) Inclusion of the canary SLA credit language Ben proposed.
3) A Dec implementation start with embedding pool migration first, then chat on a staged timeline (we prefer a Jan 15 pilot start).

If you can send the updated term sheet and a one-page implementation timeline by EOD Dec 8 we can route for procurement approval. We’ll aim to sign and kick off the pilot as soon as the terms land.

Regards,
Tom Reynolds
